core_obligations: Preserve the full Main Setting, section-dominating definition and genus/normal-bundle reduction.
Retain the author degree estimate and full Section 3: rank-one quotient, numerical scroll class and both containment cases, including uniform positive genus bound.
Retain full Section 4 Schubert rigidity proof, positive top-Chern expansion, exceptional class exclusion and line nonexistence used in the scroll argument.
Keep both degree ranges in one Theorem 1.4/4.3 claim; no split of support lemmas, cases, examples or applications.
proof_roadmap: Normal-bundle quotient degree bounds reduce hyperbolicity to genus estimates.
Separate rank distribution, then rank-one scroll containment/noncontainment cases.
Use the full Schubert-class positivity and rigidity argument for lines; combine as Theorem 4.3.
difficulty_reason: Even after the explicitly cited external normal-bundle, scroll and homogeneous-geometry tools are allowed, this author proof must control the rank-distribution cases, compute the multidegree of the quotient scroll, derive distinct lower bounds from containment in the ambient hypersurface or intersection with it, and turn these into a uniform positive genus estimate. The low-degree range requires the retained dual-Grassmannian rigidity argument and positive top-Chern Schubert expansion with exclusion of the exceptional class. These connected quantitative and geometric obligations are a nonroutine current core, rather than mere substitution into an external theorem.
